svg.text: Selected cloud: AWS | Tier 1 Digital Service: Multi-Region Reliability Architecture
Active primary + warm standby | trust boundaries, traffic flow, failure domains, security controls | [P1] to [P4] map controls to the scenario problems
TRUST BOUNDARY 1: AWS Global Edge | Failure domain: global (data plane in every edge location)
REGION 1: ACTIVE PRIMARY | Failure domain: region
TRUST BOUNDARY 2: Private VPC | Failure domains: 3 Availability Zones
Private app subnets x3 AZ | Security Groups
mTLS, IRSA, PDBs, AZ topology spread
[P2] retry budget (20% of active requests), deadlines,
TRUST BOUNDARY 3: Isolated data subnets x3 AZ | no route to internet
TLS + IAM auth | retry topics 1, 5, 30 min | DLQ topic + redrive
FQDN allowlist to provider endpoints only
REGION 2: WARM STANDBY | Failure domain: region
TRUST BOUNDARY 2: Private VPC | Failure domains: 3 Availability Zones
Private app subnets x3 AZ | Security Groups
same mesh resilience policy as primary
TRUST BOUNDARY 3: Isolated data subnets x3 AZ | no route to internet
FQDN allowlist to provider endpoints only
RELIABILITY CONTROL PLANE | cross-region, out of band from the request path
CloudWatch Alarms to SNS to on-call
Telemetry flows out of both regions; canaries probe the edge and each regional endpoint; FIS experiments target both regions.
[P1] slow detection of customer impact [P2] retry storms caused two regional incidents [P3] DR never exercised end to end [P4] unclear reliability ownership

Customer journey availability 99.99% (error budget about 4.3 min per 30 days, 52.6 min per year) | RTO 45 min via rehearsed ARC Region switch plan | RPO 5 min: async replication typically seconds, alarmed at 60s lag
AZ failures are absorbed in-region with no failover (the 99.99% budget cannot afford a 45 min regional cutover often). Istio on EKS is used because AWS App Mesh reached end of support on 30 Sep 2026
and Amazon VPC Lattice does not provide retry budgets or outlier detection; external providers sit behind fallbacks so their availability does not cap the journey SLO.
